blocks.heading: Formal Object and Admissible Domain
blocks.text: The proposed contribution is a classical general-relativistic theorem-conjecture, not an empirical inference about observed remnant demographics. Its formal object is the pair of linked propositions P1 and P2: a trapped-surface threshold theorem and the consequent exclusion of stable non-black-hole remnants above a compactness-dependent mass scale. The admissible domain is deliberately narrow. It comprises spherically symmetric, nonrotating collapse of massive stars with isotropic pressure on a globally hyperbolic, sufficiently regular spacetime, with classical matter fields obeying the Averaged Null Energy Condition (AANEC) along complete null generators. This domain boundary is essential: the theorem is not a general proof that all massive stars form black holes, and it does not by itself derive the observed 2-5 solar mass gap. That gap remains an astrophysical consistency constraint whose explanation is confounded by supernova explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, binary evolution, and pair-instability processes. The scope therefore fixes what the later derivation may and may not claim.

blocks.heading: The AANEC Focusing Relation
blocks.text:
The AANEC constraint on the stress-energy tensor T_{ab} contracted with the tangent vector k^a to null geodesic generators is proposed as the energy-positivity premise that seeds the Raychaudhuri focusing chain:

int_{lambda_1}^{lambda_2} T_{ab} k^a k^b d lambda >= 0

blocks.heading: Why AANEC Alone Does Not Close the Chain
blocks.text: The relation in the equation block is an averaged positivity statement along a null generator, and it is not a pointwise energy condition. Averaged conditions are motivated because pointwise energy conditions are systematically violated by quantum fields, so weaker averaged or inequality-based statements are required for broader validity (W3009127927). However, averaging along a generator does not, by itself, guarantee the local or integrated null convergence required to drive the expansion scalar theta of a congruence negative in finite affine parameter. This is the central conceptual gap the problem definition isolates. The plan therefore treats an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition, recorded as A5, as an independent geometric hypothesis rather than a consequence of AANEC alone. The precise mathematical form of A5, and how it is to be distinguished from A2, is not supplied upstream and must be fixed before the forward derivation can be audited.

blocks.heading: Assumption Boundary Consumed by the Next Stage
blocks.text:
The following six assumptions constitute the admissible model class. Each is a declared premise whose status is carried forward as a proof obligation or an unresolved definition rather than a verified fact:
- A1: classical General Relativity with spherically symmetric collapse and isotropic pressure (user-declared).
- A2: matter fields satisfy AANEC along complete null generators (user-declared).
- A3: global hyperbolicity and sufficient regularity for trapped-surface arguments (user-declared).
- A4: completeness of the relevant null generators (user-declared).
- A5: an explicit averaged null-convergence/focusing condition holds along the relevant generators, independent of A2 (user-declared; mathematical form missing, needs_human_input).
- A6: non-black-hole remnants are modeled as stable equilibrium objects obeying a bounded compactness or TOV-like limit (user-declared; stability predicate not formalized).

blocks.heading: Proposed Propositions and Failure Boundary
blocks.text: Two candidate propositions are proposed for the restricted model class, both unverified and pending human review. P1: if collapse satisfying A1-A5 reaches a model-dependent compactness threshold, trapped-surface formation is forced. P2: consequently, stable non-black-hole remnants above a compactness-dependent mass scale are excluded within this class. The proposed failure condition is explicit and must be tested before the chain is accepted. The theorem fails or must be restricted if AANEC is violated, if the added averaged null-convergence/focusing condition A5 fails, if null generators are incomplete, if quantum stress-energy violates ANEC, or if nonspherical, rotating, magnetic, or exotic compact dynamics evade the averaged-focusing assumptions. The mass-gap inference additionally fails or becomes non-discriminating if explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, pair-instability processes, or binary evolution dominate the observed remnant distribution. A valid counterexample must satisfy all of A1-A6 while evading trapped-surface formation; the two proposed witnesses do not currently meet this bar because A5 and the stability predicate remain ill-defined, so the counterexample search is a boundary case rather than a refutation.

blocks.heading: Scope Decisions Carried Forward
blocks.text:
| Decision | Adopted in this route | Rejected or deferred |
|---|---|---|
| Energy premise | AANEC (A2) plus independent averaged focusing (A5) | Pointwise NEC/SEC as the sole premise |
| Compactness quantity | Misner-Sharp C (D4) as the threshold variable | Any numeric threshold value |
| Mass-gap status | Astrophysical consistency constraint, confounded | Theorem-derived prediction of the 2-5 solar mass gap |
| Counterexample | Must satisfy all of A1-A6 | Witnesses that violate A5 or the stability predicate |
| Claim status | Proposed, unverified, requires human review | Proved or observed result |

claim_provenance.statement: The formal object is the pair P1/P2 within the narrow classical, spherical, isotropic, globally hyperbolic, AANEC-satisfying model class, with the observed mass gap treated only as a confounded astrophysical constraint.
AANEC is proposed as the averaged positivity of T_{ab} k^a k^b along null generators, the energy premise entering the focusing chain.

AANEC alone does not imply the local or integrated null convergence needed for trapped-surface formation; an independent averaged focusing condition A5 is required, whose mathematical form is missing.
A1-A4 fix the geometric and causal domain: spherical isotropic collapse, AANEC along complete generators, global hyperbolicity, and null-generator completeness.
A5 and A6 are declared premises whose formal content (the averaged focusing form and the stability/compactness predicate) is unresolved and requires human input.
P1 and P2 are proposed, unverified propositions: a compactness-threshold trapped-surface bound and the consequent exclusion of stable non-black-hole remnants above a compactness-dependent mass scale.

The failure condition is explicit: the theorem is restricted if AANEC or A5 fails, generators are incomplete, quantum ANEC is violated, or nonspherical/rotating/exotic dynamics dominate; a valid counterexample must satisfy all of A1-A6.

open_items.text: The template_details.assumptions field carries a canonical status of needs_human_input; the declared assumption set A1-A6 is therefore presented as a proposed boundary requiring human confirmation rather than a fixed premise.
